description: Two-panel quantitative figure for the Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel plate in six conditions. (a) is a line-with-marker plot: y-axis "GND density/ ×10¹⁴ m⁻²" (ticks 0–12, step 2), x-axis "Steels" with categories HR, IQ-1050, QA-620, QA-680, QA-740, QA-800. Black squares = BCC phase, red circles = FCC phase. Printed data labels: BCC 10.81, 8.23, 5.63, 4.93, 4.84, 4.63; FCC 8.37, 5.01, 3.39, 2.98, 2.79, 2.66 — both fall monotonically with increasing annealed temperature, and BCC lies above FCC at every condition. (b) is a grouped bar chart: y-axis "Boundary density/μm⁻¹" (ticks 0.0–2.4, step 0.4), same six x categories; legend AG Boundaries (black), High-angle Packet Boundaries (blue), Low-angle Packet Boundaries (cyan), Block Boundaries (red), Sub-block Boundaries (green). No numbers are printed on the bars. Together the panels argue that annealing progressively removes geometrically necessary dislocations while redistributing grain-boundary character from block to austenitic boundaries.

subfigures.description: Line plot of GND density (×10¹⁴ m⁻², y-axis 0–12) versus steel condition (HR, IQ-1050, QA-620, QA-680, QA-740, QA-800) for BCC phase (black squares) and FCC phase (red circles). Every point carries a printed value: BCC 10.81, 8.23, 5.63, 4.93, 4.84, 4.63 and FCC 8.37, 5.01, 3.39, 2.98, 2.79, 2.66, i.e. a monotonic decrease along the sequence with BCC always higher than FCC.

Grouped bar chart of boundary density (μm⁻¹, y-axis 0.0–2.4) for the same six conditions, with five boundary classes: AG Boundaries (black), High-angle Packet Boundaries (blue), Low-angle Packet Boundaries (cyan), Block Boundaries (red), Sub-block Boundaries (green). Black AG bars are tallest from QA-620 to QA-800, peaking just under the 1.6 gridline at QA-740 and dropping at QA-800; the red block-boundary bar is highest at IQ-1050 (a little above the 0.8 gridline) and decreases continuously across the QA series; green sub-block bars are appreciable only at HR and IQ-1050; blue and cyan bars stay small in all conditions, largest at HR.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots two series labelled BCC phase (black squares) and FCC phase (red circles) against the x-axis categories HR, IQ-1050, QA-620, QA-680, QA-740, QA-800.
Printed data labels in (a) for the BCC phase are 10.81, 8.23, 5.63, 4.93, 4.84 and 4.63 ×10¹⁴ m⁻² from HR to QA-800.
Printed data labels in (a) for the FCC phase are 8.37, 5.01, 3.39, 2.98, 2.79 and 2.66 ×10¹⁴ m⁻² from HR to QA-800.
In (a) the BCC-phase GND density exceeds the FCC-phase value at every condition, and both decrease monotonically along HR → IQ-1050 → QA-620 → QA-680 → QA-740 → QA-800.

Panel (b) is a grouped bar chart with the legend AG Boundaries (black), High-angle Packet Boundaries (blue), Low-angle Packet Boundaries (cyan), Block Boundaries (red) and Sub-block Boundaries (green).
In (b) no numeric values are printed on the bars; only relative heights against the 0.4-step gridlines can be read.

In (b) the black AG Boundary bar is the tallest class for QA-620 through QA-800, peaks just below the 1.6 μm⁻¹ gridline at QA-740 and is lower again at QA-800, while the red Block Boundary bar is highest at IQ-1050 (just above the 0.8 μm⁻¹ gridline) and shrinks continuously across the QA series.

Green Sub-block Boundary bars are only appreciable at HR and IQ-1050 and are near-zero for all QA conditions, and blue/cyan packet-boundary bars remain small in every condition with their maximum at HR.
The caption states that (a) shows the GND density and (b) the grain boundary density of the experimental steel corresponding to Fig. 7.
The citing text states that the GND density was calculated from KAM using the Burger's vector of 2.887 Å for BCC and 2.563 Å for FCC (measured by XRD) and an EBSD step size of 150 nm.

The citing text states that after quenching at 1050 °C the block-boundary density was higher than the AG-boundary density and the situation for HR was the opposite, matching the relative black and red bar heights in (b).

The citing text states that for QA specimens the AG-boundary density increased with annealed temperature but decreased at 800 °C because of some coarse austenite grains, while block-boundary density decreased continuously with annealed temperature.

The citing text states that block boundaries (>45°) contributed to the yield strength of the martensitic stainless steel and that their decrease contributed to the decrease of yield strength of the annealed specimens.

unreadable_items: panel (b): bars carry no printed numeric labels, so only qualitative ranking and position relative to the 0.4 μm⁻¹ gridlines can be reported
panel (b): green Sub-block Boundary bars for the QA-620 to QA-800 conditions are too short to quantify (may simply be absent/zero)
